newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: AMCOAL , MINORCO BUY INTO COLOMBIA.
newsitem.headline: AMCOAL , MINORCO BUY INTO COLOMBIA.

text.p: Anglo American Coal Corp Ltd said on Wednesday it had decided to purchase, jointly with Minorco Plc, a 50 percent interest in a coal mining operation in Colombia from Glencore International AG.
The sale is effective retrospectively from January 1, 1997, subject to a due diligence study which is well advanced.
The mine, with proven reserves of 250 million sales tonnes, holds the lease for the Cerrejon Centrale mining area in the Guajira region of northern Colombia.
The mine has a production capacity of some four million tonnes a year, but it is planned to increase capacity progressively to 10 million tonnes.

The cost to Amcoal -- which will have a substantial involvement in the tchnical management -- of its share of the acquisition, the expansion of the mine and the establishment of rail and port facilties will be some $145 million.
Chairman Dave Rankin said the acquisition was not expected to have material impact on Amcoal earnings until the mine reached increased levels of output.

"However, it does constitute an important initial step for Amcoal in expanding coal mining activities internationally in a country with significant potential for future development," he said in a statement.
Amcoal has registered as interested party with the Colombian government, in conjunction with Minorco, in relation to unexploited coal blocks.
